### Rationale
I verified Codex's three shapes by calling `_judge_pin_is_hit` directly with the allowlist bypassed: all three return ZERO hits — the false negatives are real at the detector level. Split argv misses because `JUDGE_PIN_FLAG_RE` fires on line 52 (`--judge-model`) which has no forbidden literal, while line 53's literal has no flag/var on its own line; shell-var indirection misses because the var is `JUDGE`, not `*JUDGE_MODEL*`; the `DEFAULT_MODEL` constant misses because its name lacks `JUDGE_MODEL`. So Codex is factually correct that the detector under-matches these shapes.

BUT the decisive question is present-time defect vs future risk, and this is unambiguously a future risk. (1) The live tree is CORRECT: all three cited files are LEGITIMATE grandfathered non-Sonnet pins (Betley gpt-4o anchors / stale-migrate Haiku), and the gate's job is to leave them alone — which it does via the exact-path allowlist (`JUDGE_PIN_LEGACY_ALLOWLIST` lines 946/948, `_SH` line 965). There is NO un-allowlisted live miss. (2) Codex's own framing concedes the future tense — each point ends "if a NEW file uses this shape, the detector won't catch it." (3) The detector is a documented assignment/call-aware line-scanner (`workflow_lint.py:837-851`), never claimed as AST-complete dataflow; Claude's two NITs and the implementer report already named the line-scanner residuals. The failure mode of the gap — a FUTURE judge pin slipping a 0-GPU-h lint — is fully recoverable (the always-on `llm-judging.md` rule, code-review, and the analyzer all backstop it); it is not "a real bug in the new surface the pipeline cannot recover from inline." Codex's required fix (extend detection + regression tests) is a hardening ENHANCEMENT beyond the shipped detector's minimal contract, not a correction of a wrong present-time verdict.

The one valid residue: the `test_live_trees_pass` docstring (line 22) overstates "grandfather-completeness invariant" — it proves only that the CURRENT detector+allowlist returns no errors, which is what Claude's PASS rested on. That is a doc/strength-of-claim gap, persisted as a CONCERN, not a blocker. Verdict: PASS (Claude was right that the shipped gate is sound for its tree; Codex was right about the detector gaps but they are future-risk hardening, not a present-time FAIL).
